strategy.summary: Reproduce the column-order rank bug in statsmodels.tools.tools.matrix_rank with method='qr'. The developer's test test_matrix_rank_column_order runs ip, qr and svd over all six column permutations of exog=[ones, x, 2x] and asserts rank 2. On the buggy commit the qr case should fail on some permutation with rank 3, while ip and svd pass. On the fixed commit (scipy.linalg.qr with pivoting=True, tol keyed to the largest diagonal element) all three pass. Build statsmodels from source at the buggy commit, apply the test diff, and run only that test.

system_packages: a C compiler (gcc or clang) and a BLAS/LAPACK provider as used by numpy/scipy wheels
build_commands: python -m pip install numpy scipy pandas pytest cython
python -m pip install -e . --no-build-isolation  (or python setup.py build_ext --inplace, per INSTALL.txt)

strategy.reproducing_test: statsmodels/tools/tests/test_tools.py::test_matrix_rank_column_order[qr] (parametrized over ip, qr, svd; the [qr] case is the one expected to fail on the buggy commit)
strategy.success_criterion: Buggy revision 1e750ab0e99c: the test_matrix_rank_column_order[qr] case fails with AssertionError on some permutation (rank 3 instead of 2, err_msg 'column order (...)'), while [ip] and [svd] pass. Fixed revision: all three parametrized cases pass, with rank 2 for every permutation of the columns.
strategy.numerical_probe: exog = np.column_stack((np.ones(40), 1e3*np.arange(1.0,41.0)/7.0, 2.0*x)); for each permutation of columns, call tools.matrix_rank(exog[:, list(cols)], method='qr') and check the result equals 2.

input_output_examples.input: exog = column_stack(ones(40), x, 2x) with x = 1e3*arange(1,41)/7, columns permuted over all six orders, method='qr'
input_output_examples.buggy_output: rank 3 for at least one column order (commit reports rank 3 in one order and rank 2 in the other five)

risks: The buggy-revision failure depends on roundoff in the Householder QR residual of the exactly collinear column (2x versus x). Whether the residual lands above the tolerance abs_diag[0]*ncols*eps depends on the BLAS/LAPACK build and CPU. If the residual rounds to exactly zero or the ordering stays benign on a given platform, the qr case may pass on the buggy revision and the transition will not occur. Record the BLAS used (e.g. OpenBLAS vs MKL) and check which permutation fails.
The test result is sensitive to the default tol formula, which is keyed to abs_diag[0]. Reproduce with the default tol (tol=None); passing an explicit tol changes the outcome.

Versions of numpy and scipy are not stated by the evidence (both constraints are null, unbounded, with no era ceiling). I chose current releases of numpy, scipy and pandas compatible with a 2023-era statsmodels source tree. If the source tree fails to build with the newest numpy, pin numpy to a release from the same era. This is a choice, not a documented requirement.
The ip and svd cases do not depend on pivoting and should pass on both revisions. Only the qr case should transition; a failure in ip or svd indicates an environment problem, not the bug.
The test file imports itertools and the new test must be applied on top of the buggy commit; the test diff itself touches only test_tools.py.

Building statsmodels requires Cython-compiled extensions. Importing statsmodels.tools without a successful build fails for reasons unrelated to the bug, so confirm the build before interpreting the test result.

oracle.reference_source: the rank property of the column space: rank must be 2 for every column permutation of exog=[ones, x, 2x] (test assertion)
oracle.why: rank is an integer, so the oracle is exact equality with 2; no numerical tolerance applies to the assertion itself

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision, the qr case computes an unpivoted QR of a permuted exog. The diagonal of R is not sorted, and tol is keyed to abs_diag[0]. For some column order the count of diagonal entries above tol is 3 rather than 2, so assert_equal(rank, 2, err_msg='column order ...') raises AssertionError for that permutation.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With scipy.linalg.qr(m, mode='r', pivoting=True), R's diagonal is in decreasing magnitude and tol is keyed to the largest diagonal element. The count of diagonal entries above tol is 2 for every permutation, so all six assertions hold and the qr case passes. The ip and svd cases pass on both revisions.
